name: showreel-c3-golden-gate

voice.text: Was the Golden Gate Bridge nearly black and yellow? Yes, America's navy wanted stripes, so ships could see it in fog. The Army's pilots wanted red and white stripes instead. But the steel arrived already coated in a red primer. Architect Irving Morrow loved it against the fog, the hills and the sea. He chose that warm colour, called International Orange. It opened in 1937, and it has stayed orange ever since. Turns out, the world's most famous orange started as primer.

caption:
The Golden Gate Bridge nearly went black and yellow. The US Navy wanted stripes so ships could see it in fog, and the Army's pilots wanted red and white. The steel arrived in a red primer, and the architect kept its warm colour. 🌉

Send this to someone who's walked across it. Which landmark should we explain next? 👇
